questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of international football
Why football fans are singing less at matches
How to write a football song
Why tickets for football matches are expensive
questions.why: Dan says the atmosphere in some stadiums is becoming quiet, as fans sing less.

questions.q: What does Neil prefer about going to a live match rather than watching on TV?
options: You can see more of the action than you can on TV
It is cheaper
You feel the atmosphere and can join in the songs
You can meet the players
questions.why: Neil says on TV you don't feel the atmosphere and can't sing along with the chants.

questions.q: Why does Dan say fans of Welling United 'might argue with you'?
options: Because Neil got the team's name wrong
To joke that Manchester United isn't the only famous United
Because Welling United won the league that year and are famous
Because he supports Manchester United
questions.why: He jokes after Neil calls Manchester United the most well-known team with United in its name.

questions.q: According to Joe Wilson, what are witty football songs often about?
options: A certain player or moment in a club's history
The other team's fans
The referee
The city where the club plays
questions.why: He says some are 'honed specifically to celebrate a certain player or moment in a club's history'.

options: To show how he supports England
To make a joke about the way Dan pronounces some English words
To show a mistake in pronunciation
To show that words get extra syllables in chants
questions.why: He shows that in a stadium the two-syllable word 'becomes three syllables'.

questions.q: What have some football managers complained about?
options: Fans are too quiet, and this affects the players
Fans sing rude songs
Stadiums are too small
Players don't sing the national anthem
questions.why: Dan says some managers complain the fans are too quiet and this has a negative effect on the players.

questions.q: According to Joe Wilson, how are football crowds changing?
options: They are much younger than they were in the past
There are more women
They are older, and tickets cost more
There are more foreign fans
questions.why: He mentions changing demographics: 'Older supporters, more expensive tickets.'

questions.q: How might stadium design reduce singing?
options: The roofs make it too loud
The stadiums are too big
Fans now sit much too far from the pitch to feel involved
All-seater stadiums may stop people standing to sing
questions.why: He says all-seater arenas 'may discourage the instinct to stand up and sing'.
